name: High Places
overview: The term 'High Places' in Scripture refers to elevated sites where people built altars and worshipped, as seen in Abraham's altar on a mountain east of Bethel and Jacob's sacrifices on a mount. While some high places were used for worshiping the LORD, such as the mount of Moriah where Abraham was commanded to offer Isaac, many became centers of idolatrous worship, including those dedicated to Baal. God explicitly condemns these high places, promising to destroy them along with their idols, reflecting His abhorrence of such idolatry and the licentious practices associated with them.
